grammar.topic: Review: 3rd and mixed conditionals, wish, past modals
explainTr: Bu hafta geçmişe dönük yapıları öğrendin: üçüncü koşul (If I had known, I would have helped), karışık koşul (If I had studied, I would be a teacher now), wish / if only ve geçmiş modallar.
Geçmiş modallar: must have (kesin çıkarım), might have (olasılık), can't have (imkânsız), should have (yapmalıydı), needn't have (gerekmiyordu). Hepsinde have + V3.
Olay raporu yazarken tarafsız ol; kimseyi suçlama. Kendi düşüncelerini 'I should have...' veya 'If I had..., ...' ile nazikçe ifade edebilirsin.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'yapsaydım, olurdu' ve 'yapmalıydım' ekle anlatılır. İngilizcede zaman farkı yapıyla gösterilir: had + V3, would have + V3, should have + V3.
table: If + had + V3, would have + V3
If I had seen it, I would have helped.
If I had studied, I would be a nurse.
must / might / can't / should / needn't have + V3

reading.title: Hafsa's first incident report
reading.text:
On Tuesday evening, Hafsa sat at her laptop and prepared to write her first official incident report. She had a clear goal: to summarize what happened in the cafeteria that day in an accurate and appropriate way. She knew that the principal and the parents would read it, so every word mattered.

She started with the facts. The incident occurred at 12:15 during lunch. A fifth-grade student named Daniel dropped his tray, and food fell on the floor. Initially, nobody noticed. A few seconds later, another student, Amy, stepped on a piece of fruit and slipped. She hit her knee on a bench. Furthermore, two other students tripped over the tray while trying to help her.

Next, Hafsa described how the adults responded. "I immediately asked the students to move back. Mr. Brown called the nurse, and a custodian cleaned the floor. Subsequently, the nurse checked Amy's knee and called her mother." Hafsa also wrote that there was no serious injury, only a small bruise.

Then she wrote about her thoughts. "If the floor had been cleaned immediately, Amy wouldn't have slipped. I should have asked for a mop right away. Daniel needn't have been afraid; he didn't do it on purpose. I wish the cafeteria had more staff during lunch."

She paused. A report should not blame anyone, she remembered. So she deleted one sentence that sounded too harsh and replaced it with a calmer one. She also marked the document "confidential," because it included names.

At the end, Hafsa listed her concerns and suggestions: more supervision, a quick cleaning procedure, and clearer rules about carrying trays. She wrote, "I believe these changes can prevent similar accidents."

When she finished, she read the report twice and corrected two small mistakes. Then she sent it to Mr. Brown with a polite message: "Please find my report attached. Let me know if you need more details." A few minutes later, he replied: "Excellent work, Hafsa. Clear, accurate, and professional." She smiled. A year ago she could not have written this in English.

questions.q: What was Hafsa's goal when writing the report?
options: To ask for a day off
To describe the incident accurately and appropriately
questions.whyTr: Metin: summarize ... in an accurate and appropriate way.

options: She slipped on food and hit her knee.
questions.whyTr: Metin: Amy stepped on fruit, slipped, hit her knee.

questions.q: Why did Hafsa delete one sentence?
questions.whyTr: Metin: too harsh; replaced with a calmer one.

questions.q: What did Mr. Brown say about the report?
options: It was clear, accurate, and professional.
questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: Clear, accurate, and professional.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Hafsa, I'm reviewing your incident report. May I ask a few questions?

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Not at all. The summary is very good. I only need one detail: what time exactly did the accident occur?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: At twelve fifteen. I looked at the clock right after it happened.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Good. And who else was involved besides Amy?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Two students tripped over the tray. They weren't hurt, but I listed their names in the report.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: That's fine, but please remember that the document is confidential. Don't share it with other parents.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I understand. Should I call Amy's mother again? She was a little worried.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Yes, that would be appropriate. Our procedure says to follow up within twenty-four hours.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I'll do that tomorrow morning. Is there anything urgent I should fix in the report?

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Just one small thing. You wrote 'I should of asked for a mop.' It should be 'should have'.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Oh, thank you! I see my mistake. I'll correct it right away.

questions.q: What detail does Mr. Brown need?
options: The exact time of the accident
questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: what time exactly did it occur?

questions.q: Why must the document be treated carefully?
questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: the document is confidential.

questions.q: What does Mr. Brown say about the procedure?
options: Follow up with the parent within twenty-four hours.
Write a new report every day.
questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: follow up within twenty-four hours.

questions.q: What mistake did Hafsa make in the report?
options: She wrote 'should of' instead of 'should have'.
questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: It should be 'should have'.

writing.promptTr: Sınıfta olan bir olayı anlatan resmi bir rapor/e-posta yaz (Mr. Brown'a veya öğretmene). Olayı sırayla anlat; hafta boyunca öğrendiğin yapıları (üçüncü koşul, karışık koşul, wish, must/might/can't have, should/needn't have) kullan. 120-180 kelime.
writing.promptEn: Write a formal incident report to Mr. Brown about an event in a classroom. Use this week's grammar: third and mixed conditionals, wish, past modals (120-180 words).
frames: Dear Mr. Brown, I am writing to report an incident that occurred ...
I should have ... / I wish ... had ...
writing.model: Dear Mr. Brown, I am writing to report an incident that occurred in my classroom on Tuesday at 10:30. Initially, the students were working quietly. Then a boy named Jacob dropped a bottle of water, and the floor became wet. A girl, Maya, slipped and hurt her elbow. Subsequently, I sent a student to the nurse, and the nurse responded within five minutes. Fortunately, Maya only has a small bruise. If I had checked the floor earlier, I would have seen the water. I should have asked for a mop immediately. Jacob needn't have been so afraid, because it was an accident. I wish the room had more paper towels. Furthermore, I suggest a clear procedure for spills. I believe it can prevent similar accidents. This report is confidential. Please contact me if you need more information. Sincerely, Hafsa Odabasi
checklistTr: Resmi selam ve kapanış var mı?
Olayı sırayla (initially, subsequently, furthermore) anlattın mı?
En az üç farklı hafta konusu yapısı kullandın mı?
Kimseyi suçlamayan, nesnel bir dil kullandın mı?

Why did she mark it confidential?

Yesterday, Ms. Carter's class went on a short field trip. A student forgot his lunch, and Hafsa shared hers. "I needn't have packed so much," she laughed, "but I'm glad I did."

What does Hafsa mean?
